transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Dubois, thank you for coming back in to speak with me. I have something important and difficult to discuss regarding the care of your daughter and your grandchild.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. Please. I am still very anxious about the baby.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am here because I made a mistake. Two hours ago, I reviewed the fetal heart rate tracing and I categorized it incorrectly. I missed the significance of the decelerations, which are the drops in the baby's heart rate. I apologize to you and your family. It was my responsibility to read that correctly, and I failed to do so.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You... what? You made a mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, I did.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And the baby? Is the child hurt because you failed?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: A second clinician reviewed the trace two hours later and identified the severity of those drops. We acted immediately once that was caught. Does that make sense so far, or can I explain that differently?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It makes sense. It makes sense that you were careless. C'est inadmissible. My daughter is in that room trusting you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand this is a very difficult moment to process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Difficult? It is a betrayal of trust. My family, we believe in the dignity of the profession. To hear you simply... forgot to look properly?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I accept full responsibility for this error. There is no excuse for missing those decelerations.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel as though I am speaking to a wall. Do you even realize the terror of thinking your grandchild was in danger because of a clerical error?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You say you understand, but you have the face of a stone. Je suis profondément blessé. Do you have any idea how this feels for us?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize this is a distressing situation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Distressing. That is a very small word for this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am truly sorry that this happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And now? What happens now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are continuing to monitor the baby closely.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan. What is the specific plan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep a close eye on the readings.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Which readings? Who is looking at them? For how long?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The nursing staff and the attending physician are overseeing the telemetry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And if it happens again? If you make another mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will see how the baby progresses over the next few hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is not enough. I want to know exactly what is being done to ensure my grandchild is safe right now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The baby is stable at the moment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stable is not a plan. I want a written guarantee. I want to know who is in charge.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The attending doctor is in charge of the unit.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And when will they speak to me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: They will likely come by later.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Later? What is later? Two hours? Four hours?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am not sure of the exact time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot believe this. You admit you failed us, and then you tell me you do not know when I will see the person in charge.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry you feel that way.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not feel it, I know it. My dignity is not something you can just ignore while you apologize.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You keep saying that. But you are not listening to me. You are just waiting for me to stop talking.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am listening.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, you are waiting. There is a difference.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I apologize for the error in the tracing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, the error. The error was the beginning. Now the error is the silence and the lack of a plan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are monitoring the heart rate.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is what you said before. Give me a time. Tell me exactly what the next step is.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will check with the attending.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I will stay here until I have a name and a time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish their turns and remains regulated under significant pushback, with no interruptions or rushing language.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the first turn using lay language, and a comprehension check was performed once ('Does that make sense so far...').

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language, accepts full personal responsibility, and maintains this accountability throughout the patient's anger.

R.justification: The resident relies exclusively on generic validation ('I understand', 'I realize this is a distressing situation') without naming specific emotions or engaging the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders and vague statements ('monitoring', 'will see how the baby progresses', 'soon') with no timelines or specific plan.
